title: A Federated Universal Domain Generalization Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Global Prototype Alignment and Decision Boundary Collaborative Optimization
abstract: The health status of industrial sensors often determines whether production equipment can operate effectively over the long term. In recent years, the development of federated domain generalization diagnosis methods has not only ensured data privacy among different industrial sectors, but also effectively addressed domain shifts in cross-condition diagnosis. However, due to drastic changes in industrial environments, differences in label spaces across different domains frequently occur. Therefore, this paper focuses on a practical and novel industrial diagnosis scenario, namely federated universal domain generalization, and proposes a diagnostic framework based on Global Prototype Alignment and Decision Boundary Collaborative Optimization (GPA-DBCO) to effectively identify private classes and unknown faults. First, by introducing domain-adversarial training and prototype alignment, the model is guided to learn domain-invariant feature representations that are insensitive to changes in working conditions. Second, a cross-client unknown fault prototype library is constructed on the server side to simulate potential unseen new fault types, thereby training a universal classifier. Finally, a distance–entropy-based joint optimization strategy for decision boundaries is designed, enabling the model to accurately identify common faults, private faults, and unknown faults simultaneously when deployed in an unknown target environment. Experiments were conducted on a sensor dataset from a nickel flash smelting furnace system, and the results verified the superiority and effectiveness of the GPA-DBCO diagnostic method.

title: Horizontal federated spectral clustering via tensorized low-rank aggregation
abstract: Federated clustering provides significant advantages in protecting data and information privacy. However, most existing federated clustering methods focus primarily on K-means and matrix factorization, while exploration of federated spectral clustering remains substantially limited. Furthermore, current approaches often fail to explicitly model the latent similarities and divergences among data distributions across different clients. To address these gaps, we introduce a Horizontal Federated Spectral Clustering via Tensorized Low-Rank Aggregation (HFSC-TLA) framework that effectively captures cross-client relationships by constructing a global dictionary. Specifically, each client decomposes its local feature space to reconstruct pairwise affinities, thereby implicitly approximating the kernel matrix required for spectral clustering without violating privacy constraints. During server-side aggregation, we impose a low-rank constraint on the stacked local dictionaries to distill a shared subspace across clients, while learning adaptive fusion weights to accommodate client heterogeneity. We also present guarantees of differential privacy. Comprehensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that HFSC-TLA consistently outperforms baselines. These results validate the advantages of jointly modeling similarity reconstruction, rank-constrained aggregation, and adaptive weighting in federated settings.
